doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why Uptown Blues was given to him and became the theme
summary: Young thinks Lunceford chose him over Wilson and Paul Webster, and the tune became Lunceford's theme song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right, right. Why, whose decision was it for you to solo on Uptown Blues? Who was the bandleader?

That‘s a good question; I think Jimmie Lunceford was, because I think, yeah well, I tell you how that possibly happened now that I think about it. Gerald Wilson, myself, and Paul Webster…they gave it to me because I played better solos, not better I won‘t say that either, but I, how can I explain that because they didn‘t give it go Paul, they gave it to me, told me to play. And they didn‘t give it to Gerald; it was just us three trumpets in them days. I don't know why they gave it go me because…
They made the right decision though. [laughs]

I think so. I think they, I really do, I think they made the right decision because that became one of the best things that I ever, well not one of the best things that I ever did, but more popular. I recorded with all the bands—Count Basie—all of the bands and everything, but it was never like Uptown Blues for some reason.
So did Jimmie keep this as a feature for you?
Yes, in fact, he made that into a theme song. He made it because he used to have another theme song he played, I can‘t think of it, but anyway he turned that into his theme song.
